findings.claim: Qualitative Coding has a finished grounded-theory result on a rights-clear general corpus the workbench can read
findings.note: Schema 3 package on 25 Open Science interviews: 8 categories, 6 propositions; the 90 distinct passages its theory cites all resolve to QC segments (S1 receipt). Their offsets match the Zenodo text once one file's CRLF line endings are normalised (Q14, resolved).

findings.claim: Some repository in ~/code2 already measures text quantitatively, so the workbench can consume it
findings.note: No such capability; QC's quantitative follow-up only returns conceptual_follow_up_only. The workbench owns the S2 adapter; which category it measures is Q15.

findings.claim: QC's qualitative path has been validated by an outside researcher
findings.note: QC's roadmap step 5 is not done. Plan #8 states validation as agreement with the corpus author's own coding.

findings.claim: Process Tracing's answer path can take a QC handoff and give the workbench a gated export
findings.note: Only the frozen pipeline (pt/) accepts --qualitative-handoff and writes pt_export_v2 with a publication gate. The answer path, the draft-audit prototype (ADR 0004), takes no handoff and writes no pt_export_v2 (Process Tracing Q20). S4 adds the handoff input and Q20's partial adapter in process_tracing (Q23).

findings.claim: Theory Forge offers a consumer export the workbench could read for 1.0
findings.note: No consumer export; roadmap stale. Moved after 1.0 in Plan #8.

findings.claim: A second rights-clear corpus with its authors' own coding is identified for the benchmark
findings.note: Chosen in S6 under Q19's rule: it must differ in subject, research team and coding tool or export format.

findings.claim: The repository already decided how the first quantitative-text strand must be validated
findings.note: Word-list count baseline mandatory; dummy and TF-IDF baselines; language model a challenger with behavioural tests; feasibility readout first; accuracy alone prohibited. The brief was never approved (status line :4). Plan #8 S2 adopts it condition by condition and names the two it cannot meet (Q16).

findings.claim: The workbench owns one general investigation record that keeps a study's question, evidence, runs, findings, reviews and next actions together
findings.note: The map makes it the product's centre; the only implementation is hard-coded to the PsychosisBank investigation (investigation_id is a fixed literal).

findings.claim: Process Tracing's pt_export_v2 carries a publication gate the workbench can require before showing a causal conclusion
findings.note: PublicationGateV2.publishable exists in PT; the workbench's current pt_export_v2 reader reads only comparative_conclusion.public_headline_eligible, so S4 extends it.

findings.claim: QC's 8 grounded-theory categories rest on 8 distinct sets of evidence
findings.note: Two pairs of categories cite exactly the same two incidents (Traceable... with Corrective...; Terminological... with Attributed reuse...), so 8 categories rest on 6 distinct sets of cited turns. The two categories 'open data' qualified for are distinct, so the construct choice is unaffected; the study page says so (plan S2).
